lxc_6170b04c240a7a9b.text: Cologne’s story connects the city today and a little history with Cologne Cathedral, the bridge, the Old Town, and the museums by the river.

lxc_757ea63e935a2e18.text: Modern life includes Kölsch, Carnival, and trade fairs, while winter brings the Christmas markets.

lxc_01317d009eb4647d.text: Cologne is a large German city on the Rhine, the river that runs through it.

lxc_ab1170cd142d02a3.text: With over 1 million people, Cologne is Germany’s fourth-largest city.

lxc_7e5e0acd7d673f79.text: It is also the largest city in North Rhine-Westphalia, the German state where it stands.

lxc_0e99213c266336c9.text: The state capital is Düsseldorf, about 35 kilometres northwest of Cologne.

lxc_6a642ad8c498e9a2.text: Most of Cologne lies on the left bank of the Rhine.

lxc_fa94bf8b3f21ede0.text: The river is an important part of the city’s setting, but Cologne offers more than river views.

lxc_0ead64b168ad7ca0.text: It has more than 30 museums and hundreds of galleries.

lxc_ca456a0ded43e948.text: Its mix of older places and newer buildings gives the city a varied appearance.

lxc_704084118f305968.text: The Romans founded Colonia Claudia Ara Agrippinensium, the Roman settlement here, in AD 50.

lxc_69209963e0651f1d.text: They named it after Emperor Claudius, a Roman ruler, and his wife Agrippina, who was born here.

lxc_d58bf2040f4c3e05.text: The name Cologne comes from Colonia.

lxc_a821f1c2368f8413.text: In the Middle Ages, Cologne was a rich trade city on the Rhine.

lxc_077ad4ace55568c3.text: It joined the Hanseatic League, a group of trading cities.

lxc_32b69fa7a6b71615.text: The river connected the city with other places and their goods.

lxc_e289ea0009244f19.text: Much later, bombing during the Second World War destroyed around 80% of the old city centre.

lxc_6518f1f1562fbf73.text: Cologne was rebuilt after the war.

lxc_bc70287fb5b265cc.text: Today, Roman remains and medieval churches stand alongside many newer buildings from the rebuilding.

lxc_4ac095a95347feff.text: The centre is not simply an old city preserved unchanged.

lxc_a816de699987aa3c.text: Cologne Cathedral, also called Kölner Dom, is a Catholic church in the Gothic style.

lxc_910ef94764cac88d.text: Building began in 1248, stopped around 1560, and finished in 1880 according to the medieval plan.

lxc_57190bf57eb46add.text: The full span was 632 years, including the long pause.

lxc_5f91fc3045820978.text: Its two spires are 157 metres tall, making it the world’s tallest twin-spired church.

lxc_cd08346c57e58bf5.text: It was built to hold the Shrine of the Three Kings, a golden medieval shrine.

lxc_f042fef5cf6b0b2d.text: In 1996, it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site, a place recognized for its special cultural value.

lxc_5a7205030f4a434c.text: It is Germany’s most visited landmark, with about 6 million visitors a year.

lxc_30fc128ead5b0e2f.text: Fourteen bombs hit it during the Second World War, but it stayed standing.

lxc_3895a8b1bc80d1a8.text: Visitors can climb 533 steps in the South Tower to a viewing platform about 100 metres high.

lxc_b34e92187ce5e514.text: The route passes the bell chamber.

lxc_226a1a5a2a0d5fab.text: Since 1 July 2026, tourist visits inside require a ticket.

lxc_90ff10a7a908f3d6.text: People coming to pray can still enter free through the entrance facing Cologne Central Station.

lxc_adf3300a9348997c.text: The Hohenzollern Bridge is a railway bridge across the Rhine next to the cathedral.

lxc_1a321a1789260149.text: Built from 1907 to 1911, it carries more than 1,200 trains a day.

lxc_dfc777937cce3150.text: It is Germany’s busiest railway bridge.

lxc_3a2dafe995ecc419.text: Since 2008, couples have attached love locks, padlocks that express their love, to its fence.

lxc_c0f64808a04a2a99.text: The Old Town, Cologne’s historic central area, includes the squares Alter Markt and Heumarkt near the Rhine.

lxc_ed448a058a698445.text: A riverside walk offers a different way to enjoy this part of the city.

lxc_42e4a73d227b463a.text: At Rheinauhafen, a harbour on the Rhine, the Chocolate Museum follows 5,000 years of chocolate history.

lxc_14a54a1b1bb00d86.text: Visitors can see cocoa plants in a 10-metre-high tropical house, watch chocolate being made, and enjoy the café’s river view.

lxc_17d2bd53e4a23644.text: Museum Ludwig, a modern art museum next to the cathedral, has a building that opened in 1986.

lxc_c3ce7b6f98e48fdd.text: It has Pop Art, art connected with popular culture, and around 900 works by the artist Pablo Picasso.

lxc_e27b259cc7cdbeec.text: Its Picasso collection is the world’s third-largest, after Barcelona and Paris.

lxc_556900d7b46fb6a6.text: Its name has been protected in the European Union since 1997, and real Kölsch must be brewed within about 50 kilometres of Cologne.

lxc_7c465d0fc7ef79be.text: It comes in a Stange, a tall, thin 200 ml glass.

lxc_f5ce94fd9c4fa785.text: A Köbes, the waiter, carries glasses on a round tray.

lxc_edfb492483ae8fa3.text: The waiter brings another when yours is empty and marks each drink on your beer mat, the small mat under your glass.

lxc_241f9f20985890cc.text: Putting the mat on top means you want to stop.

lxc_83157ba7744dcaa9.text: Cologne Carnival is called the fifth season, the city’s special carnival period.

lxc_0085cab2bc37984f.text: Street carnival runs from Weiberfastnacht, the Thursday before Lent, to Ash Wednesday, the start of Lent.

lxc_728a542ec3ec419e.text: Its highlight is the Rose Monday parade, two days before Ash Wednesday.

lxc_3ae375198c725898.text: The local greeting is Kölle Alaaf.

lxc_b9e0d0018e507fb1.text: Koelnmesse, Cologne’s trade fair centre, holds around 80 trade fairs a year.

lxc_07c4769ba9c7c5e4.text: A trade fair brings businesses and visitors together around a subject or industry.

lxc_504d7148056ab3a9.text: One example is gamescom, the video game fair.

lxc_909c2f0b12794a47.text: RTL, Germany’s largest private broadcaster, also has its headquarters here.

lxc_3805de962f8f5eab.text: Cologne opened its first Christmas market in 1820.

lxc_e454407c93da367a.text: Today, its Christmas markets attract about 4 million visitors a year.

lxc_7ee19ecab1951cf3.text: These seasonal markets sell food, gifts, and decorations among Christmas lights.

lxc_745c3f3beee959d1.text: The Market of Hearts is on Roncalliplatz, the square in front of the cathedral.

lxc_8e44eb6309acded2.text: In 2026, it runs from 16 November to 23 December, with more than 140 stalls and a stage beneath a tent of lights.

lxc_5f5e890bdaad08ba.text: The Market of Angels is on Neumarkt, a central square near the main shopping streets.

lxc_f0d2a67d4e350c9d.text: Stars shine in the trees, and people dressed as angels walk through the market.

lxc_29fc3bf48a984f86.text: Heinzels Wintermärchen, another market, spreads across Alter Markt and Heumarkt.

lxc_2c5e64e6783899a3.text: It takes its name from the Heinzelmännchen, little house elves in a Cologne legend.

lxc_2abd0dcacc049ca5.text: It opens on 23 November 2026, and its Heumarkt area stays open until 10 January 2027.

lxc_6b0e43c4050a2d6b.text: There is a large open-air ice rink for skating on Heumarkt and a Christmas Ferris wheel at the Chocolate Museum.

lxc_dbdcef167d3752bd.text: Visitors can enjoy waffles and Glühwein, hot red wine with spices.

lxc_7fc10b9cb697614c.text: The Christmas Market Express, a small train, takes people between markets.
